admin.access.this_none: This connection shows no device certificate – it can only be switched on from a device with a certificate. If one is installed and the browser does not ask: close all browser windows and open it again (it remembers the last choice, including «Cancel»).

admin.backup.auto_hint: Create a folder festpos-sicherung on a USB stick and plug the stick into a Pi. That Pi writes an encrypted backup into it right away and then every 15 minutes (with the backup password above) and keeps the last 20 there. It puts the Fully APK next to them once (not encrypted, only when it is new). The stick is mounted only while writing and can be pulled out at any other time. Overview and status display show when the last backup was made; with a single Pi they warn when a backup is missing. Restore as above.
admin.backup.dl_hint: Everything included – data, credentials and keys – encrypted with a password you choose here (at least {count} characters). Don’t store the password next to the file.
admin.backup.dl_short: The password needs at least {count} characters.
admin.backup.restore_confirm: All current data will be replaced by the backup. Continue?
admin.backup.rs_hint: Replaces all data. New Pi: keys and credentials also come from the backup, then the Pi restarts. Same Pi: this Pi’s keys and credentials stay. A checklist appears afterwards.
admin.backup.rs_hint_files: On the stick (folder festpos-sicherung): «festpos-a-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS» are the automatic backups of Pi A – the newest is at the bottom and needs no password on this system. «festpos-manuell-…» or «festpos-sicherung-…» are downloaded ones with their own password.
admin.backup.rs_info_auto: Automatic backup (USB stick) of Pi {pi} · {at} · version {app}
admin.backup.rs_no_camera: No camera available – type the password.
admin.backup.rs_not: This is not a FestPOS backup.
admin.backup.rs_own: The Pi first tries its own backup password – usually nobody needs to type anything.
admin.backup.rs_own_manual: Downloaded with its own password – the Pi first tries its backup password, otherwise it asks for the one chosen when downloading.
admin.backup.rs_pw_needed_manual: Password needed – the one chosen when downloading
admin.backup.rs_restart: The keys from the backup are being installed and the Pi restarts. This page reloads by itself afterwards (about 1–2 minutes).
admin.bon.blk.beep_hint: The printer beeps when a ticket arrives. Printers with buzzer only; always at the end.
admin.bon.blk.check_hint: Checksum of the receipt. Always last.
admin.bon.blk.datetime_hint: Date and time of the order.
admin.bon.blk.delivery_hint: When to serve (Products › Serving times). «Now» is the first entry; with «not for Now», BREAK, END … stand out on normal tickets.
admin.bon.blk.footer_hint: E.g. thanks or website – only appears with text.
admin.bon.blk.guest_hint: Only above CHF 400 with VAT – entered in the administration when printing.
admin.bon.blk.head: Event and printer
admin.bon.blk.head_hint: Event name on the left, printer name on the right.
admin.bon.blk.header_hint: As it should appear on the receipt – the first line in bold.
admin.bon.blk.image_hint: Own image, dithered in black and white like the logo (max. 3).
admin.bon.blk.info_hint: Date and time (always), table, order number, handheld; with «Separate» the person.
admin.bon.blk.logo_hint: Ticket logo, dithered in black and white.
admin.bon.blk.qr_hint: E.g. website or donation, with a short text below (max. 3).
admin.bon.blk.r_top_hint: Only when needed: COPY on every further print, TEST in test mode. Always at the top.
admin.bon.blk.rule_hint: Separator line across the full width.
admin.bon.blk.sum_hint: Total (if the printer shows prices), number of items and the order number.
admin.bon.blk.t_items_hint: What to prepare; cancelled items struck through below.
admin.bon.blk.t_top_hint: Only when needed: TEST (practice order), REPRINT, «Redirected» (printer standing in). Always at the top.
admin.bon.blk.table_hint: So the kitchen sees the table from afar. When split, «1 of 3» next to it.
admin.bon.blk.text_hint: Own text anywhere – e.g. thanks, a note about next year.
admin.bon.blk.time_hint: Time of the order and which handheld (who) ordered.
admin.bon.blk.title: RECEIPT and number
admin.bon.blk.total_hint: Total, rounding for cash and how it was paid.
admin.bon.blk.vat_hint: Only appears when VAT is switched on.
admin.bon.blk.vat_no_hint: Only appears when VAT is switched on (Checkout).
admin.bon.blocks_hint: In print order. Drag at ⋮⋮ or directly in the preview to move (keyboard: Alt+↑/↓). The eye switches on and off.
admin.bon.image_hint: PNG, JPG or WebP. Dithered in black and white like the logo. The image is only kept with «Save».
admin.bon.logo_app: Logo of the administration (Event) – no own ticket logo
admin.bon.logo_hint2: PNG, JPG or WebP. The thermal printer only prints black: ideally a single-colour logo with clear lines on a white or transparent background. Without a ticket logo, the administration logo applies.
admin.bon.logo_remove_confirm: Remove the ticket logo? Then the logo of the administration applies again (if any).
admin.bon.p.caption: Text below
admin.bon.p.part: «1 of 3» next to the table number (otherwise below)
admin.bon.p.prices: Print prices (all kitchen and drinks tickets)
admin.bon.preview_tap: Tap to select the block · exactly as printed (sample data, not saved yet)
admin.bon.reset_confirm: Reset all blocks to the template? The receipt header and footer stay. Nothing is saved until «Save».
admin.bon.rules_receipt: REQUIRED blocks can be moved and styled but not hidden. COPY/TEST is always at the top, the check number always last.
admin.bon.rules_ticket: REQUIRED blocks can be moved and styled but not hidden. TEST, REPRINT and «Redirected» are always at the top. The design applies to all kitchen and drinks tickets.
admin.bon.sample_hint: Prints an example with these blocks (including unsaved ones), «SAMPLE» at the top. No receipt and no number is created.
admin.bon.sample_no_printer: No printer switched on – set one up under Devices & network › Printers.
admin.bon.unsaved_more: Applies from the next ticket; existing receipts stay as they were.
admin.bon.when_hint: Ticked = this serving time is printed large on the ticket. The serving times are under Products › Serving times.
admin.bpw.hint: All backups are encrypted – the automatic ones on the USB stick with this password. Without it, a backup can’t be restored on a new Pi. Print it and keep it with the emergency password.
admin.bpw.new_done: New backup password created – please print it.
admin.bpw.new_q: Create a new backup password? It applies from the next backup. Older backups on the stick still need the previous one – keep the old printout.
admin.bpw.p_case: Upper/lower case doesn’t matter, dashes may be left out.
admin.bpw.p_foot: Keep with the emergency password, not with the Pi and not on the stick. If a new backup password is created, older backups still need this one.

admin.bpw.p_s3: Type the password or scan the QR code with the handheld.
admin.bpw.p_s4: The Pi restarts. Then go through the checklist.
admin.bpw.p_what_text: All automatic backups on the USB stick (folder festpos-sicherung) are encrypted with this password. Without it, a backup can’t be restored on a new Pi.
admin.bpw.title: Backup password
admin.cardw.abort_q: Cancel writing? The card will then be empty and must be written again.
admin.cardw.busy: An event is running (open tickets or orders in the last half hour). Writing takes 5–15 minutes and slows this Pi down – better after the event.
admin.cardw.cancelled: Cancelled – the card for Pi {pi} is empty.
admin.cardw.card_hint: Plug the USB card reader with the new SD card into Pi {pi} (this Pi writes). Everything on the selected card will be erased.
admin.cardw.done: Card for Pi {pi} is ready, the card reader has been ejected.
admin.cardw.erase: Everything on the card {card} ({size} GB) will be erased.
admin.cardw.failed_hint: The card is empty. Try another card or another card reader; the way via a PC (card package) still works.
admin.cardw.h_card: Plug the card reader into Pi {pi}
admin.cardw.here_hint: USB card reader on Pi {pi} – no PC and no internet needed.
admin.cardw.l_new: New Pi for operation with 3 Pis
admin.cardw.l_spare: Spare card – joins and fetches the data from the other Pis
admin.cardw.l_spare_single: Spare card for this Pi – then restore a backup
admin.cardw.missing: A program is missing on this Pi: {list} – install the new version with setup.sh.

admin.cardw.next_spare_single: Unplug the card reader. Shut down Pi {pi}, swap the card, switch on and restore the newest backup from the stick under Maintenance › Backup.
admin.cardw.not_in_use: Not during operation: writing takes 5–15 minutes and slows this Pi down.
admin.cardw.open_hint: The Pi writes a new card in the USB card reader – for Pi B/C or as a spare card, without a PC.
admin.cardw.progress_hint: Do not unplug the card reader. The page may be closed – writing continues.

admin.cardw.r_system: system disk of this Pi – never
admin.cardw.running_warn: Pi {pi} is running. Do not use the old card of Pi {pi} afterwards – two cards with the same letter disrupt operation.
admin.cardw.searching: Searching for card readers every 3 seconds.

admin.closing.cash_hint: Count and enter the cash. Card and TWINT are pre-filled with the amounts recorded at the till (including tips) – compare with the SumUp and TWINT statements and correct if needed. Expected cash = float + turnover (+ tips) − card − TWINT − other − Payrexx.
admin.closing.check_bad: Warning, changed afterwards: {list}. These orders no longer match their checksum.

admin.closing.check_other_key.one: {count} entry was created with an earlier key (e.g. before a reinstallation) and cannot be checked here.
admin.closing.check_other_key.other: {count} entries were created with an earlier key (e.g. before a reinstallation) and cannot be checked here.

admin.closing.confirm: Create daily closing: {count} orders, revenue {amount}? These orders can then no longer be changed or cancelled.
admin.closing.confirm_no_count: Close without counted cash? The cash count will then be missing from the closing.
admin.closing.created: Daily closing no. {no} created. PDF and CSV are available below.
admin.closing.late_book: Guest did not pay cash – book it
admin.closing.late_book_q: The guest did not pay cash (the amount was missing in the cash of that closing). Book it now? The next closing counts the card payment and expects correspondingly less cash.
admin.closing.late_hint: Check the cash of that closing: if exactly this amount is missing there, the guest did not pay cash – book it. If the cash was right, the guest paid twice – refund in the Payrexx account.
admin.closing.late_refund_q: The guest paid cash, so twice. Has the full amount been refunded in the Payrexx account? The cash stays as it is.

admin.closing.late_title.one: A card payment was only reported as paid after the closing – the order had been closed as cash. Please decide:
admin.closing.late_title.other: {count} card payments were only reported as paid after the closing – the orders had been closed as cash. Please decide:

admin.closing.no_payment_mode: The payment method is not recorded at the till (Checkout). Everything is listed under “Not recorded” and counts as cash.
admin.closing.nothing_open: There are no orders since the last closing.
admin.closing.open_hint: Orders from {from} to {to}. Practice orders are not counted.

admin.closing.open_tabs.one: {count} table is still open. The daily closing is only possible once it is settled or written off as «not paid».
admin.closing.open_tabs.other: {count} tables are still open. The daily closing is only possible once all are settled or written off as «not paid».

admin.closing.payrexx_waiting.one: One card payment is still open. The daily closing is possible once it is confirmed on the phone or cancelled here.
admin.closing.payrexx_waiting.other: {count} card payments are still open. The daily closing is possible once they are confirmed on the phone or cancelled here.

admin.closing.pw_cancel_q: Cancel this card payment? Only if it is not paid in the Payrexx app. If “paid” arrives afterwards, it will appear here for a decision.
admin.closing.tip_formula: Expected cash = float + turnover + tips − card − TWINT − other − Payrexx − tips paid out. Card, TWINT and other are pre-filled including tips, as on their statements.
admin.closing.verify_other_key: made with an earlier key – cannot be checked here

admin.devices.apk_failed: did not arrive 3 times today – do it by hand with “Update Fully” in the device view
admin.devices.apk_newer: Fully {version} is newer than the APK on the Pis ({apk}) – nothing to do.
admin.devices.apk_open_busy: order pending – tried again as soon as the handheld is free
admin.devices.apk_open_unreachable: not reachable – tried again when it next connects
admin.devices.apk_play: Fully {version} from the Play Store – updates through the Play Store, not with the APK on the Pis.

admin.devices.bad_name: Name: 1 to 30 characters – letters, digits, spaces, dot and hyphen.
admin.devices.blocked_hint: Blocked devices can no longer reach the ordering app and are missing from the status display. A fixed IP stays recorded and applies again after unblocking. “Delete permanently” (admin) removes the device and its fixed IP from the list – the block remains.
admin.devices.certs_off: Device certificates are switched off (PHONE_CERTS=0 in festpos.conf): any device on the Wi‑Fi can order.
admin.devices.data_hint: With a fixed IP the device appears on the status display.
admin.devices.data_hint_access: The device only gets a device certificate: no fixed IP, no Fully.
admin.devices.data_hint_fully: The handheld’s IP is added in the last step (Fully shows it then) and becomes its fixed IP. The device certificate gets the same name.
admin.devices.data_hint_reset: Suggestion: next free IP. The Pi gives it to the handheld via DHCP once it has scanned the QR. The device certificate gets the same name.
admin.devices.delete_hint: Removes the device from the list and the status display and forgets the Fully access. A valid certificate is blocked (you will be asked). Admin only.
admin.devices.delete_revoke_hint: Once blocked, the handheld can no longer order at once. Without blocking, the device stays in the list with its valid certificate.
admin.devices.deleted_cert_kept: “{name}” removed from the status display – the certificate is still valid, so the device stays in the list.
admin.devices.dup_hint: Several devices have the same name ({count}). Please open the device and rename it, or block the one no longer used – otherwise tickets and the status display are ambiguous.
admin.devices.dup_how: Another device is also called “{name}”. Give this device its own name below, or block the one no longer used.
admin.devices.fully_cert_expires: The certificate of the Fully remote admin expires on {date}. After that the Pi can no longer reach this handheld (not even to renew the device certificate): beforehand, use “New Fully certificate” and put the file on the handheld.
admin.devices.fully_hint: The one-time password is valid for 30 minutes. The real Fully password never goes unencrypted over the Wi-Fi.
admin.devices.fully_none: Fully is not yet set up on this handheld.
admin.devices.fully_s1: Install Fully Kiosk Browser from the Play Store and open it.
admin.devices.fully_s2: In Fully: Settings › Remote Administration › turn on Enable Remote Administration and Remote Admin from Local Network, port {port}, and enter this one-time password as Remote Admin Password:
admin.devices.fully_s3: Enter the handheld’s IP (shown in Fully under Remote Administration) and “Start setup” – FestPOS then switches to the real password.
admin.devices.ip_pending: The handheld currently still has the address {ip}. It gets the fixed IP at the next Wi-Fi renewal (within a few minutes) – immediately by turning Wi-Fi off and on.
admin.devices.ip_remove_q: Remove the fixed IP of “{name}”? The device no longer appears on the status display; Fully access and the fixed Wi-Fi assignment are forgotten.
admin.devices.ip_used: The IP {ip} is already used by another device.
admin.devices.k_access_sub: Device certificate only, used in the normal browser. For spare devices or tests.
admin.devices.k_fully_sub: The handheld stays as it is. Fully is installed as a normal app, the certificate is set up.
admin.devices.k_reset: Set up a new handheld (factory reset)
admin.devices.k_reset_sub: The handheld is reset. Fully is installed as device owner; afterwards the handheld is locked to FestPOS. Setup via QR code on the welcome screen.
admin.devices.licence_how: Fully is not licensed yet (device ID {id}). Single licence: at license.fully-kiosk.com assign it to this device ID or move the licence to it, then “Restart Fully”. Volume licence: store it under Devices & network › Settings › “Setup QR”.
admin.devices.link_expired: Link expired. Create the certificate again.
admin.devices.link_left: Link valid for {time} more minutes, can only be used once.
admin.devices.list_hint: Role and “In use” apply immediately. Battery, connection and Fully status are on the status display; everything else about a device under “Edit”.
admin.devices.mac_alarm_both: This device certificate reports from two Wi-Fi addresses (MAC) at the same time. Either the certificate was copied or two handhelds are using it. The fixed IP is therefore not reassigned.
admin.devices.mac_alarm_how: If you know which handheld is the right one: take or keep its MAC – the other gets no fixed IP. If nobody knows: block the device and set up the right handheld again.
admin.devices.mac_alarm_taken: This device certificate reports from a Wi-Fi address (MAC) that belongs to the handheld “{other}”. The fixed IP is therefore not reassigned.
admin.devices.mac_alarm_title: Two devices with the same certificate
admin.devices.mac_ask: The handheld reports with a new Wi-Fi address (MAC) {mac} (currently address {ip}). The fixed IP is not reassigned automatically (Devices & network › Settings › Fixed IP on new MAC: off).
admin.devices.mac_ignored: The Wi-Fi address {mac} was rejected and does not get the fixed IP. It will not be reported for 24 hours.
admin.devices.mac_keep_confirm: Leave the fixed IP of “{name}” with {old}? The Wi-Fi address {mac} gets no fixed IP.
admin.devices.mac_kept_done: Fixed IP of “{name}” stays with the previous MAC.
admin.devices.mac_known: Wi-Fi address (MAC) of the handheld: {mac} – the Pi always gives it this IP.
admin.devices.mac_minutes_hint: If a handheld reports with its device certificate but a new Wi-Fi address (MAC), the Pi moves its fixed IP to the new MAC – as soon as the old one has not been active for this long. If both are active at the same time (copied certificate or two handhelds), there is an alarm in the overview and under “Handhelds & PC” instead.
admin.devices.mac_random: The handheld uses a randomised Wi-Fi address (MAC). Better choose “Handheld MAC” instead of “Randomised MAC” on the handheld under Settings › Wi-Fi › FestPOS Wi-Fi › Privacy. If it changes anyway, the Pi takes over the new MAC by itself.
admin.devices.mac_take_confirm: Move the fixed IP of “{name}” to the Wi-Fi address {mac}? The old one ({old}) will no longer get it.
admin.devices.mac_taken_done: Fixed IP of “{name}” reassigned – the handheld gets it within 1–2 minutes.
admin.devices.mac_unknown: Fixed IP not reserved yet: the handheld’s Wi-Fi address (MAC) is not known yet. As soon as the handheld connects with its device certificate (order app open), the Pi takes it over by itself.
admin.devices.mac_unknown_nocert: Fixed IP not reserved yet: the handheld’s Wi-Fi address (MAC) is not known yet. It is added when setting up with Fully or with a device certificate (New certificate).
admin.devices.mac_wait: The handheld reports with a new Wi-Fi address (MAC) {mac} (currently address {ip}). If the old MAC stays quiet, the fixed IP moves to the new one at {time}.
admin.devices.name: Device name
admin.devices.name_in_cert: The name is in the device certificate and cannot be changed here. The fixed IP is used for the status display and the Wi-Fi assignment (DHCP); empty = remove from the status display.
admin.devices.name_rename_hint: The name is in the device certificate. A new name gives the same device a new certificate (the role stays): with Fully it reaches the handheld by itself, otherwise via QR code. The fixed IP is used for the status display and the Wi-Fi assignment (DHCP); empty = remove from the status display.
admin.devices.need_fully_pw: The Fully password is not set yet (Devices & network › Settings).
admin.devices.need_qr: The setup QR is not configured yet (Fully APK and Wi-Fi under Devices & network › Settings).
admin.devices.need_wlan: The FestPOS Wi-Fi is not set yet (Devices & network › Settings). If the handheld is already on the Wi-Fi, just continue.
admin.devices.new_cert_confirm: Create a new certificate for “{name}”? The old one stays valid until the handheld uses the new one for the first time – then the server blocks it.
admin.devices.no_cert_hint: This device has no device certificate yet and so cannot reach the ordering app.
admin.devices.none: No devices yet. Set up the first one with “Add device”.
admin.devices.pair_after: Then open the ordering app. Chrome asks once which certificate to use: choose “{name}”.
admin.devices.pair_pc: Download here on the PC instead
admin.devices.pair_step1: Scan the QR code with the camera app and open the link. The file is downloaded.
admin.devices.pair_step2: Tap the file or: Settings › Security and privacy › More security settings › Install from device storage › VPN and app user certificate.
admin.devices.pin_hint: Without its own PIN the shared one applies (Checkout & app › Ordering app › PIN lock). Time lock and «lock when the screen was off» apply to all. The handheld checks the PIN even without a connection; a new one applies after 20 seconds at most.
admin.devices.pin_remove_q: Remove the own PIN of «{name}»? The device then uses the shared PIN again.
admin.devices.qr_copying: Not ready: Fully APK is still being copied to the Pis
admin.devices.qr_hint: Applies to all new handhelds set up under Handhelds & PC › “Add device” › “Set up a new handheld (factory reset)” – none of this is asked there. The Wi-Fi is in the “FestPOS Wi-Fi” card.
admin.devices.qr_no_apk: Not ready: no Fully APK uploaded yet (card “Fully APK”)
admin.devices.qr_no_url: Not ready: APK address or checksum missing
admin.devices.qr_ready_net: Ready – APK from the internet, Wi-Fi “{ssid}”
admin.devices.qr_ready_pi: Ready – APK from this Pi, Wi-Fi “{ssid}”
admin.devices.qr_secret: The QR contains the Wi-Fi password: only show it on screen, do not photograph or print it.
admin.devices.reboot_confirm: Restart the handheld “{name}”? It will be gone for about a minute.
admin.devices.remove_confirm: Delete “{name}” permanently? The device disappears from the list; its certificate stays blocked. A new device with this name needs a new certificate.
admin.devices.rename_confirm: Rename “{old}” to “{name}”? The device gets a new certificate for this.
admin.devices.renamed_scan: New certificate for “{name}” – scan the QR code with the device.
admin.devices.renew_auto_hint: The Pi renews handhelds with Fully itself as soon as the certificate is this close to expiry and the handheld is not in use. The old certificate stays valid until the handheld uses the new one. Handhelds without Fully show “Renew now” in the ordering app.
admin.devices.renew_auto_how: The Pi installs a new certificate via Fully as soon as the handheld is not in use – nothing to do on the handheld.
admin.devices.renew_failed_how: Automatic renewal did not work today (step {step}: {detail}). The Pi will try again tomorrow – or now with “Renew now”.
admin.devices.renew_fully_how: Automatic renewal is off (Devices & network › Settings › Validity): use “Renew now” here – Fully receives the new certificate via remote admin.
admin.devices.renew_manual_how: Without Fully the Pi cannot install the certificate itself: tap “Renew now” in the ordering app on the handheld, or use “New certificate” here and scan the QR code.
admin.devices.reset_noqr: Handheld already set up and on the Wi-Fi: continue without QR

admin.devices.tap_sent: version {version} sent on {time} (not confirmed by Fully)

admin.plan.row_bad: «Numbers from» must end with a number, e.g. 13 or T1

admin.plan.row_done.other: {count} tables inserted – selected together, now drag them into place

admin.plan.save_failed: not saved – change again or reload the page
admin.plan.start_number_hint: keypad first, plan via the switch
admin.plan.start_plan_hint: switch «Plan | Number» at the top; the handheld remembers the last chosen view
admin.plan.start_title: Table selection on the handheld starts with
admin.plan.title: Table plan
admin.plan.unplaced_none: all tables are in a plan
admin.printers.add_hint: Epson TM-T20III: set a fixed IP in the printer’s web interface. Port 9100 is the default. In the kitchen, “Print prices” is usually off.
admin.printers.delete_confirm: Delete printer? Products using this printer will no longer print a ticket.
admin.printers.name: Name
admin.printers.none: No printer yet. Add the first one with «+ Printer».
admin.printers.st_no_status: Reachable, but no status reply – paper and cover cannot be checked.
admin.printers.st_paper_low: Paper almost out – have a roll ready.
admin.printers.st_setup_hint: Epson TM-T20III: set «Busy condition» to «Receive buffer full» in the printer settings (ANLEITUNG, «Drucker einrichten») – then it reports paper and cover.
admin.printers.st_silent: Printer not responding – check paper and cover. Tickets wait until it responds again.
admin.printers.st_unreachable: Unreachable ({error}). Check power, network cable and IP.
admin.printers.test_sent: Test print is on its way. If nothing comes out: check IP, cable and paper.
admin.printers.vlan_hint: Printers in their own VLAN cannot be reached from the Wi-Fi – only the Pis can print. This needs a switch with VLAN (802.1Q). Each Pi sets up its address in the printer network by itself.
admin.printers.vlan_missing_hint: A Pi without an address in the printer network cannot print. Check on the Pi: journalctl -u festpos-druckernetz (cable, VLAN on the switch).
admin.printers.vlan_off_confirm: Turn off the printer network? If the printers are still in the VLAN, the Pis can no longer reach them – move the printers back to the normal network first.
admin.printers.vlan_switch: On the switch: Pi ports in VLAN {vlan} tagged (they stay untagged in the normal network), printer ports only in VLAN {vlan} untagged (PVID {vlan}). In the printer network the Pis have the addresses {pis} – do not use these for printers.
admin.printers.vlan_warn_outside: Printer “{name}” has the address {host} – it is not in the printer network {net}. Set an address from {net} in the printer’s web interface and enter it here for the printer.
admin.printers.vlan_warn_pi: Printer “{name}” has the address {host} – a Pi needs it in the printer network. Please choose another one (e.g. .20).
admin.products.categories_hint: The colour appears as a stripe on the product tiles. Without its own colour, a category automatically gets one from the series (“automatic”, ↺ = back to automatic). Individual products can get their own colour in the “Colour” column above (↺ = back to the category colour).
admin.products.category_delete_confirm: Delete category? The products remain and will then appear under “Other”.
admin.products.color_auto_title: Automatic colour from the series (depends on the order)
admin.products.delete_confirm: Delete “{name}”? Existing orders are kept. Tip: switching off “Active” only hides it.
admin.products.grp_hint: Order as in the ordering app – drag within the category
admin.products.list_hint: Changes are saved immediately. Inactive products do not appear in the ordering app. Handhelds pick up changes within a minute or via “Reload (app and price list)”. Replace an image: click on it; × removes it.
admin.products.name: Name
admin.products.new_hint: Single ticket: a separate ticket is printed for each item (e.g. meal vouchers). Without a printer, the default printer prints (Devices & network › Printers). Options (e.g. “2 sugars”, free text) are set in the list below via the “Options” column. Many products at once: import CSV.
admin.products.none: No products yet. Add one above or import a CSV file.
admin.products.sort_az_q: Reset the order of all categories and products alphabetically? Afterwards you can drag them freely again.
admin.receipt.copy_done: Copy of receipt no. {no} is printing on {printer}.
admin.receipt.dialog_hint: Prints whatever of this order has no receipt yet. If everything already has one, copies are printed.
admin.receipt.recipient: Recipient (name, address) – only needed above CHF 400 with VAT
admin.receipt.rules: Every receipt gets a consecutive number; its content is recorded and secured with a checksum. Printing again gives a COPY (also recorded). All receipts appear in the daily closing and in the log. VAT is only shown on the receipt if it is switched on above – then with VAT number, rate per item and VAT amount. Above CHF 400 a VAT receipt also needs the guest’s name and address: enter them here in the admin when printing.
admin.reset.hint: Only possible once all orders are in a daily closing. The closings (figures, PDF, CSV) and the log are kept, as are the price list, printers and tables. The orders and print jobs are deleted.
admin.reset.title: After the event
admin.restore.apk_done: Fully APK taken from the stick
admin.restore.apk_wait_sub: This Pi is fetching it from Pi {pi} – takes about a minute.
admin.restore.apk_warn: Fully APK missing on this Pi
admin.restore.apk_warn_sub: If it is on the USB stick (folder festpos-sicherung), take it from there – otherwise upload it under Devices & network › Settings › “Fully APK”.
admin.restore.dca_bad: Different certificate authority than in the backup
admin.restore.dca_bad_sub: Handhelds can’t get in: take the keys from the backup (below) or set up all handhelds again.
admin.restore.dca_manual: Device certificates: place an order with a handheld
admin.restore.dca_manual_sub: Older backup without identifier – an order shows whether the handhelds get in.
admin.restore.dca_ok_sub: Same certificate authority – handhelds order without setting up again.
admin.restore.dhcp_warn_sub: {written} of {count} – check again in a minute.
admin.restore.dkey_ok_sub: The device CA key is present (also for automatic renewal).
admin.restore.dkey_warn_sub: No new device certificates and no automatic renewal.
admin.restore.keys_cluster: With 3 Pis, replace them the same way on all cards (Devices & network › Pi › Prepare spare card).
admin.restore.keys_differ: Keys in the backup differ from this Pi’s
admin.restore.keys_q: Take certificates, keys, CLUSTER_SECRET and emergency password from the backup? Update keys are never taken over (only by hand, see the manual). The Pi restarts afterwards; the previous ones stay next to them on the boot partition.
admin.restore.keys_single: Take them if wanted: choose the same backup again, the Pi restarts afterwards.
admin.restore.keys_wait_sub: The Pi restarts for this – reload this page after about 2 minutes.
admin.restore.lkey_ok_sub: Orders and closings with the same key.
admin.restore.lkey_warn_sub: CLUSTER_SECRET differs from when the backup was made – take the keys or enter the old value in festpos.conf.
admin.restore.m_new_sub: New Pi: also check internet and router.
admin.restore.m_orders_sub: Handhelds send what is still waiting on them; add paper orders afterwards.
admin.restore.m_test_sub: As it was in the backup. Each handheld switches practice on by itself.
admin.restore.m_try: Print a test ticket, order with a handheld, look at the status display
admin.restore.receipts_new: Last in the backup: {last}. New Pi – receipts after the backup are unknown, so it continues with {next}. Whoever knows the last paper receipt can set it higher.
admin.restore.receipts_same: Last in the backup: {last}. It continues without a gap at {next}.
admin.restore.sca_ok_sub: Handhelds and Fully keep trusting the Pi.
admin.restore.sca_warn: Server certificate differs from the backup
admin.restore.sca_warn_sub: Handhelds and PCs show a certificate warning until the keys are taken over or ca.crt is installed again.
admin.restore.secrets_missing_sub: Enter them again – they were not in the backup (older version).
admin.restore.time_bad_sub: The Pi’s clock differs from this device or is before the last order.
admin.restore.title: Checklist after restoring
admin.restore.usb_warn: No recent backup on a USB stick
admin.restore.usb_warn_sub: Plug in a stick with the folder festpos-sicherung.
admin.roles.admin_only: Only the Admin role may change settings, users and roles, backup and update.
admin.roles.name: Role name
admin.roles.protect: Viewer, Event management and Admin are fixed. The Admin role can neither be changed nor deleted, and the last active admin stays: nobody can lock themselves out.
admin.save.leave_q: Changes are not saved yet. Discard and continue?
admin.settings.default_printer_hint: For products without a printer. “Automatic” uses the printer that was added first.
admin.settings.delivery_hint: Per product in the product list (“Serving time” column): off, selectable, required or only certain times. The first entry is the default. Each time gets its own tickets with a large notice; single tickets are counted per time (e.g. “End” 1/5 … 5/5).
admin.settings.event_name: Name (printed at the top of every ticket)
admin.settings.language_hint: Applies to handhelds and administration as long as no other language is chosen there, and to tickets and the status display. Each printer can have its own ticket language.
admin.settings.phones_hint: Applies to all handhelds within 20 seconds (immediately when the app is reloaded).
admin.settings.show_history: Show order history (button at the top right)
admin.settings.show_recent: Show recently served {many} below the input
admin.settings.staff_qr: Scan the table by QR code (staff)
admin.settings.staff_qr_hint: On: QR symbol at the bottom left of the table selection, the introduction shows scanning. Reads the table cards (Tables page) and – with QR ordering at the table – also the guests' QR codes: one code per table is enough. Off (default): ✕ there, clears the whole input.
admin.settings.swipe: Swiping changes the category (left/right in the product area)
admin.settings.table_word: Term in the app and on the ticket
admin.settings.tutorial_auto: Introduction starts automatically when the device name is entered or changed on a handheld
admin.setup.cert_hint: Did the browser warn about the certificate? That is expected: it is temporary and only for the setup. Compare the fingerprint with the screen at the Pi. Afterwards the Pi creates the real certificates.
admin.setup.code_hint: The code is shown on the screen at the Pi and in the file festpos-einrichtung.txt on the card’s boot partition (readable on a PC). Address of this Pi: {ips}
admin.setup.done_backup: After the restart the Pi restores the backup data by itself (checklist in the administration).
admin.setup.done_s1: Restart the Pi (button below) and connect it to the event network.
admin.setup.done_s3: Install the certificate once on every handheld and PC: {url}
admin.setup.file_hint: Copy the newest backup from the USB stick (folder festpos-sicherung) to this device and choose it here. Password: from the printout (automatic backup) or the one chosen when downloading.
admin.setup.key_hint: Save the certificate authority key (ca.key) now – it does not go on the card and is deleted after the restart. Put it on a USB stick and keep it: it is needed later to renew the server certificate.
admin.setup.net_dhcp: The Pi hands out the addresses to the handhelds (DHCP)
admin.setup.net_hint: The handhelds reach FestPOS at {vip}. The defaults match the event network in the ANLEITUNG.
admin.setup.pi_letter_sub: Letter of the Pi this card replaces
admin.setup.pi_three_sub: Spare card in operation with 3 Pis: joins and fetches the data from the others.
admin.setup.pw_hint: The admin logs in to the administration with it (user «admin») as long as there are no other users. At least 10 characters, keep it safe.
admin.setup.restart_q: Restart the Pi now? Afterwards it is reachable at the new address.
admin.setup.rtc_no_sub: The Pi does not charge the battery.
admin.setup.rtc_yes_sub: Raspberry Pi RTC battery (ML-2020): the Pi charges it.
admin.setup.sum_hint: Then the Pi restarts and has the addresses above – connect it to the event network.
admin.setup.sum_upd_own: from the FestPOS project and with own key
admin.setup.time_take: Use the time of this device
admin.setup.time_tz: Time zone Europe/Zurich (summer and winter time automatically).
admin.setup.title: FestPOS – Pi is not set up yet
admin.setup.upkey_hint: Without an own key, this Pi accepts the signed updates of the FestPOS project (the key for them is in the image). If you build and sign your own versions, choose your festpos-update.pub here – it applies in addition.
admin.setup.way_backup_sub: Replacement for a Pi: keys, passwords and data from a backup (.festpos).
admin.setup.way_cards_sub: Pi B or C for operation with 3 Pis – with the card package of Pi A (Devices & network › Pi › Expand to 3 Pis).
admin.setup.way_neu_sub: First Pi (Pi A). The Pi creates certificates and keys itself.
admin.setup.zip_hint: On Pi A: Devices & network › Pi › Expand to 3 Pis › Download card package, choose it here.
admin.stock.col_title: Sold out, or remaining quantity counted down with each order
admin.stock.hint: From “Warn at”, the status display reports the remaining quantity and the handhelds show it on the tile. Empty = no warning. Practice orders in test mode do not count; a cancellation does not add stock back.
admin.stock.on_hint: counts down with each order, at 0 the product is sold out
admin.stock.soldout_hint: the tile turns grey on all handhelds, no more tickets are printed
admin.stock.title: Stock: {name}
admin.system.hint: After shutting down, only unplug the power once the green light on the Pi has stopped flashing. Orders and tickets stay saved.
admin.system.notice_sent: All handhelds, the status display and the administration now show a message with a countdown. It can still be cancelled in the red bar at the top.
admin.system.one_hint: Only this Pi – the others keep running (notice only on the status display and in admin).
admin.system.ph_restart_app: Restart the app on the handhelds
admin.system.phones_at: The handhelds receive the command at {time}.
admin.system.phones_hint: The handhelds first show the message and receive the command shortly before the Pis. If a handheld refuses, it simply keeps running.
admin.system.phones_hint_off: To switch the handhelds on again: press and hold the power button on the handheld.
admin.system.phones_none: Including handhelds only works with Fully Kiosk (Administration › Devices & network › Handhelds & PC).
admin.system.poweroff_text: FestPOS is then off: no orders, no tickets, no status display. To switch on again: briefly unplug the power and plug it back in.
admin.system.reboot_at: Restarting at {time} – everything is back after about two minutes.
admin.system.reboot_text: No orders and no tickets for about two minutes. The handhelds keep waiting orders and send them afterwards.
admin.system.tap_pi: Tap a Pi: status, set up its screen, restart or shut down – only this Pi.
admin.system.title: Pi
admin.tables.bon_cards_text: Alternative without an office printer: one card per table with a QR code, printed directly on a ticket printer.
admin.tables.create_hint: Numbers can be typed directly in the ordering app. Named tables appear under “All tables”.
admin.tables.mode_hint: Upper/lower case is matched to the registered tables. As long as no tables are registered, “Free choice” always applies.
admin.tables.mode_strict_hint: Only the tables registered here. App and server reject unknown ones.
admin.tables.mode_warn_hint: For an unknown table the app asks (“Typo?”); ordering remains possible.
admin.tables.pdf_hint: Staff: scan with the QR button in FestPOS
admin.tables.pdf_text: A4 with 6 cards per page (large table number, QR code, event name in the club green). Print on the office printer, cut along the lines and put into table stands or laminate.
admin.tables.qr_off_ask_lead: QR scan on the handheld is switched off – the cards are only useful once an admin switches it on (Checkout & app › Ordering app). Continue anyway?
admin.tables.qr_off_done: QR scan on the handheld switched on
admin.tables.qr_off_text: The table cards are only useful once the ordering app can scan tables by QR code (Checkout & app › Ordering app). Switch it on now?
admin.tables.qr_off_title: QR scan on the handheld is off
admin.tables.staff_qr_off: QR for staff is off (Checkout & app › Ordering app): the ordering app shows ✕ instead of QR. These cards only help with QR switched on.
admin.tables.staff_qr_on: QR for staff is on. With QR ordering at the table its QR codes are enough too (Checkout) – they work for guests and staff.
admin.tabs.card_hint: Every handheld may order at every table – the order goes onto the open table. Settling on the handheld only works with a connection. In the administration, event management can always transfer open tables, settle them or write them off as «not paid» (Operation › Open tables). The daily closing is only possible when no table is open; there the payment method is split according to the payments of the table.
admin.tabs.hint: Orange: nothing ordered for a long time. «Transfer»: another handheld takes over the table (battery empty, shift change). «Settle»: the open remainder counts as paid (with the chosen payment method), the table is closed. «Not paid»: everything open is booked as cancellation «Not paid» (without cancellation tickets) – only without payment. Everything is in the log.
admin.tabs.idle: Hint «nothing ordered for a long time» after
admin.tabs.mode_off: Checkout › Settling up is set to «Immediately»: new orders do not stay open.
admin.tabs.mode_open_hint: orders add up at the table, settled at the end (after each order also «Settle now»)

admin.tabs.open_box.one: {count} table is open (CHF {amount}). The daily closing is only possible once it is settled or written off.
admin.tabs.open_box.other: {count} tables are open (CHF {amount}). The daily closing is only possible once all are settled or written off.

admin.tabs.settle_hint: The open remainder of CHF {amount} counts as paid, the table is closed.
admin.tabs.transfer_hint: This handheld takes over the table and may settle it.
admin.tabs.unpaid_hint: Everything open is booked as cancellation «Not paid» (counter-entry, shown in the daily closing), the table is closed.
admin.tabs.who: Who may settle an open table
admin.tabs.who_own: Only the handheld that opened the table
admin.tabs.who_own_lead: This handheld and handhelds of the event management
admin.tap.off_hint: Only needed when Checkout › Card/TWINT (Payrexx) is switched on.
admin.test.delete_confirm: Delete {count} practice orders? Real orders are kept.
admin.test.enable: Allow test mode on the handhelds
admin.test.exit_sent: Test mode is being ended – the handhelds take it over within 10 seconds.
admin.test.hint: For practising before the event: on the handheld under ☰ › Start test mode – or at the end of the introduction. In test mode every screen has a yellow and black border and TEST MODE is shown at the top. Practice orders count nowhere (overview, status display, export). When the app starts it is always off; it can also be ended in the status display and under Handhelds & PC.
admin.test.pin_required: Require test PIN (without a PIN anyone serving can start test mode – orders in test mode do not count)
admin.test.print: Print practice orders (tickets clearly marked TEST)
admin.test.title: Test mode (practice)
admin.time.bat_restart_off: charging off from the next restart
admin.time.browser_wrong: This device’s clock is earlier than the last order – check this device’s clock or set the time by hand.
admin.time.clock_bad: Time of the Pi – please check
admin.time.dev_clock_how: With the time server set via USB, the Android handheld gets the time from the Pi.
admin.time.dev_clock_unknown: Handheld clock: no report yet (the order app reports it when it starts).
admin.time.dev_clock_wait: The handheld has not asked the Pi yet – turn Wi-Fi off and on or restart the handheld.
admin.time.dev_ntp_at: set via USB on {date} at Pi {node}
admin.time.dev_usb: Set time server via USB (Android only)
admin.time.hint: The Android handhelds get the time from the Pi (time server via USB, Handhelds & PC › device). With Internet the Pi gets the time itself; the handhelds never set the Pi.
admin.time.manual_before_orders: This time is before the last order. Set it anyway?
admin.time.manual_confirm: Set the time on all Pis to {time}?
admin.time.manual_hint: Sets the time on all Pis (time zone of the Pi). Only needed if this device itself has no correct clock.
admin.time.never: The time has never been confirmed.
admin.time.next: Next check: after a restart from {restart}, otherwise on {date}.
admin.time.st_rtc_drift: RTC off by {span} – did not keep the time
admin.time.title: Time
admin.time.usb_adb_on: Turning on USB debugging via Fully …
admin.time.usb_how: On the handheld, at “Allow USB debugging?” tap Always allow from this computer and Allow. The Pi sets the clock and then turns debugging off again. Takes a few seconds.
admin.time.usb_how_manual: First turn on USB debugging on the handheld: Settings › About handheld › Software information › tap “Build number” 7×, then Developer options › USB debugging. Then plug in and confirm “Allow USB debugging?” with Always allow from this computer. The Pi turns debugging off again at the end.
admin.time.usb_plug: Now plug the handheld into a Pi with the USB cable
admin.time.usb_skipped: skipped – do it later under Handhelds & PC
admin.time.usb_st_timeout: No handheld detected on the USB cable (USB debugging on? adb installed on the Pi?)
admin.time.usb_st_wait: Waiting for the handheld on the USB cable …
admin.time.w_cluster: The clocks of the Pis differ from each other.
admin.time.w_never: The time has never been confirmed.
admin.time.w_old: Last confirmed on {date} – please confirm again.
admin.time.w_restart: Last confirmed on {date}, restarted since then.
admin.time.w_unsure: Pi {pis}: the RTC did not keep the time (battery?) – clock not set since start.
admin.update.back_hint: All Pis switch from version {from} to the backup {to} – again one after the other. The data stays.
admin.update.by_usb: Started with a USB stick at {time}.
admin.update.cancel_q: Cancel the update? Pis that are already done keep the new version.
admin.update.forward_hint: The backup holds version {to} (after switching back). All Pis switch from {from} back to it.
admin.update.from_net: From the internet ({source}), fetched by {name} at {time} (stored on Pi {pi}).
admin.update.from_usb: From a USB stick on Pi {pi} at {time}.
admin.update.lost: Connection briefly lost – this Pi is probably restarting. The update continues.
admin.update.net_download_q: Download version {version} now? The Pi will be online for a few minutes.
admin.update.net_found_hint: Running here: {version}. To download, the Pi goes online briefly again ({via}).
admin.update.net_hint: FestPOS fetches festpos.zip and festpos.zip.sig from the latest release of the repository and checks the signature as for an upload. The Pi is online only briefly to search and download; afterwards the internet is off again. Distribute with “Roll out to all Pis”. Not during operation.
admin.update.net_loaded: Version {version} downloaded and checked, internet off again. Continue under “Install a new version” with “Roll out to all Pis”.
admin.update.net_no_tether: Phones via USB tethering are not used – USB-A network adapter with cable to the router.
admin.update.net_no_usb: No USB network adapter found – plug it in and connect the cable to the router.
admin.update.net_no_wlan: This Pi has no Wi-Fi switched on. After updating to this version and a restart it is available (the radio stays off except for updates).
admin.update.net_none: No newer version: latest release {tag}, running here {version}.
admin.update.net_off: Internet for updates is switched off (Devices & network › Network & internet).
admin.update.net_verifying: Internet off. Checking signature and package …
admin.update.net_via_lan: Via the FestPOS network (router with internet, e.g. mobile router)
admin.update.net_via_usb: USB network adapter on the Pi (cable to a router with internet, DHCP)
admin.update.net_via_wlan: Wi-Fi of the Pi (e.g. phone hotspot or home Wi-Fi)
admin.update.new_hint: Select the ZIP (festpos.zip) and its signature (festpos.zip.sig). Signing is done on the PC with your update key; without a valid signature no Pi accepts the package.
admin.update.no_helper: The update service (festpos-update) is missing on this Pi. Install this version once by hand (update.sh) – after that it works here.
admin.update.no_key: No update key on this Pi. Set it up once: create a key on the PC and copy festpos-update.pub to the boot partition of every Pi – see the guide «Setting up the update key».
admin.update.ph_cancelled: Cancelled. Pis that were already done keep the new version.
admin.update.ph_done: Done: all Pis are running version {version}.
admin.update.ph_failed: Stopped: the update failed on Pi {pi}. Pi {pi} is running the previous version again; the others are unchanged.
admin.update.ph_failed_one: Stopped: the update failed. The Pi is running the previous version again.
admin.update.ph_running: Pi {pi} is being updated – ordering and printing continue via the other Pis.
admin.update.ph_unreachable: Waiting: Pi {pi} is not reachable. As soon as all Pis are running, it continues.
admin.update.pick_both: Please select both files: festpos.zip and festpos.zip.sig.
admin.update.start_busy: An update is already running – wait for it or cancel it first.
admin.update.start_q:
Roll out version {version} to all Pis?

One after the other, the printing one last. Each Pi is away for about a minute; the others take over ordering and printing. If it fails on a Pi, that Pi switches back by itself and the rollout stops.
admin.update.usb_handed: USB stick at {time}: version {version} checked and taken over.
admin.update.usb_hint: Copy festpos.zip and festpos.zip.sig to a USB stick (top level or folder «festpos-update») and plug it into a Pi. Once it has been read, the stick can be removed right away; the update is rolled out to all Pis as here.
admin.update.usb_installed: USB stick at {time}: version {version} installed on this Pi.
admin.update.usb_installing: USB stick at {time}: FestPOS was not running – version {version} is being installed on this Pi only …
admin.update.usb_none: USB stick at {time}: no update found (festpos.zip and festpos.zip.sig).
admin.update.usb_old: USB stick at {time}: version {version} is already installed.
admin.update.usb_unreadable: USB stick at {time}: not readable (use FAT32, exFAT or NTFS).

admin.update.w_orders.one: {count} order came in during the last {minutes} minutes.
admin.update.w_orders.other: {count} orders came in during the last {minutes} minutes.

admin.update.warn_go: Start anyway? (Each Pi is away for about a minute, the others take over.)
admin.update.would_update: Getting version {version}: Pi {pis}. One after the other, the printing one last.
admin.uplink.bad_host: Router IP address missing or invalid
admin.uplink.hint: Shows the mobile router’s signal on the status display (bars, readings, history) and warns when the signal is weak or the connection is lost. FestPOS only reads and never changes anything on the router. Access only via HTTPS: user and password are sent only when the router shows the certificate accepted here.
admin.uplink.inactive_hint: Not in use: not queried and not shown on the status display. Access and certificate stay saved.
admin.uplink.name: Name
admin.uplink.now_off: Mobile router not in use – no longer on the status display
admin.uplink.pin_changed: Caution: the router shows a different certificate than the accepted one – user and password were not sent. Only accept it if the certificate on the router was renewed on purpose:
admin.uplink.pin_new: The router shows this certificate (SHA-256 fingerprint). Compare it with the fingerprint on the router (last setup command) and accept it:
admin.uplink.raw: Router answer (without SIM and modem identifiers)
admin.uplink.setup_hint: Paste into the router’s terminal (WinBox or WebFig › Terminal) and replace PASSWORT. Creating the certificate takes a few seconds. If the router does not know «rest-api» (older version), leave that part out.
admin.uplink.title: Mobile router (optional)
admin.uplink.trust_confirm: Accept the certificate? FestPOS will then send user and password to this router.
admin.users.delete_confirm: Delete {name}? This person can then no longer log in.
admin.users.emergency: Emergency login: user “admin” with the password from festpos.conf is always Admin – even if nobody remembers their password. Only give this password to the event management or the person in charge of the technology.
admin.users.name: Name

app.tour.pay_modes: “Split”: the total is divided by the number of people – everyone pays the same. “Separate”: each person pays only what they ordered. You tap their items and take payment person by person.
app.tour.pay_next: “Next order”: back to table selection. The last table is ready to tap at the top.
app.tour.pay_total: After sending, payment comes straight away – the tickets are already on their way. At the top the total (cash rounded to 5 centimes). Below you type what the guest gives, or tap a note: the app shows the change.
app.tour.pin: PIN lock: if the handheld is not used for a while or the screen was off, the app locks. Enter the PIN to continue – nothing is lost. The event management has the PIN.

app.tour.recent: Here are the {many} you served last – one tap and you’re back there, e.g. for a second round.
app.tour.scan: Or scan the QR code on the {word}: tap this button and hold the code in front of the camera – the {word} is then selected.
app.tour.send: Send: the tickets are printed at once (kitchen, bar …). Then you go straight to payment.
app.tour.status: The dot at the top right shows whether everything is running. Green: all good. Orange: wait a moment, e.g. an order is still being sent. Red: server or printer has a problem – tap to see what. Orders are never lost, even without Wi‑Fi: they wait on the handheld. If one is rejected, ⚠ appears at the top.
app.tour.stock: Grey with “sold out”: no longer available, tapping does nothing. “3 left” and similar: only that many left – the app won’t let you order more. This applies at once on all handhelds.
app.tour.table_input: Type the {num} with the big keys. Typo? ⌫ deletes the last digit. Then tap the green button at the bottom – it shows the {word} so you can check it once more.
app.tour.test_later: Can be changed later: ☰ at the top left › Test mode. You’ll find the introduction there too.
app.tour.test_text: To practise after the introduction: all orders are practice orders, count nowhere and are not charged. {print} The screen has a yellow and black border. End it at any time in the yellow bar at the top – the next time the app starts it is off by itself.
app.tour.tile: Tap a product = 1 more. The green number shows the quantity; − at the bottom right makes it one less.
app.tour.welcome: In about 2 minutes you’ll see how to take orders and payments. Examples only: nothing is ordered and nothing is printed. You can stop at any time – “Skip introduction” at the bottom.
app.tour.when: ⏱ Delivery time: for some products you choose when they should come, e.g. “{later}”. A long press opens the choice. Each time gets its own tickets.

srv.web.tpl_privacy:
# Controller
{name}, {email}

# What data
For an order at the table we only store the order, the table, the amount and the payment reference – no name. Payment is processed by Payrexx AG (Thun); their privacy policy applies there. We never see card data.

# Purpose
To fulfil the order, for accounting and, if necessary, refunds.

# Retention
As long as accounting rules require (in Switzerland usually 10 years).

# Disclosure
Only to Payrexx for the payment. The site loads nothing from other servers and sets no advertising or tracking cookies.

# Your rights
Access, correction and deletion under the Swiss Data Protection Act (FADP): {email}.

As of: {date}
srv.web.tpl_refund:
# Refunds
If a paid order cannot be fulfilled (sold out, malfunction), we refund the full amount automatically to the means of payment used. If an order is cancelled in full or in part, we refund the corresponding amount. Depending on the means of payment, the credit takes a few days.

# Delivery
We deliver only on site during the event «{event}» to the table whose QR code was scanned. No shipping.

# Contact
Questions: staff on site or {email}.
srv.web.tpl_terms:
# 1. Scope
These terms apply to orders placed via the QR code at the table at the event «{event}» organised by {name}.

# 2. Contract
The contract is concluded as soon as the payment is confirmed and the order number is shown.

# 3. Prices and payment
All prices in Swiss francs (CHF). Payment is made immediately online via Payrexx (TWINT, card, Apple Pay, Google Pay).

# 4. Delivery
Only on site during the event: we bring the order to the table whose QR code was scanned.

# 5. Refunds
If we cannot fulfil a paid order (e.g. sold out), the amount is refunded automatically to the means of payment. For questions, ask the staff or write to {email}.

# 6. Law and jurisdiction
Swiss law applies. Place of jurisdiction is the seat of {name}.
